title: Tectonic observability Terraform adapter: unified Prometheus/Grafana + OTEL + log-forwarder
creator: Elliot Park
description: Background: Private (VPC) customers have divergent observability IaC across accounts: multiple TF modules, fragile upgrade paths, and manual health gating for collector/log-forwarder changes. Goal: deliver a single Terraform adapter ("Tectonic" observability adapter) that composes a Prometheus + Grafana stack, an OpenTelemetry collector deployment, and a resilient log-forwarder configuration with automated schema migrations and health gates. The adapter must support air-gapped deployments, per-tenant ingress controls, and an upgrade strategy that preserves dashboards, Prometheus TSDB retention, and OTEL pipeline compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioned Terraform module can deploy Prometheus, Grafana, OTEL collector, and fluentbit/forwarder into a VPC with a single module invocation
Module supports a declarative 'storage' abstraction that can be configured for s3-compatible remote_write or local PVC and includes automated TSDB retention migration steps
OTEL collector config templates support route-based sampling and are generated from a module variable without manual edits
Rolling upgrade path between major collector config versions without data loss and with automated health gating (readiness + series-validated checks)
Grafana dashboards are deployed as configmaps/helm values and preserved across upgrades; migration plan exists for UID collisions
End-to-end smoke tests (metrics ingestion, alerting rule firing, log forwarding, dashboard rendering) pass in a staging VPC before production rollout
Module has < 5% additional P95 latency impact on core inference endpoints in smoke test profile when OTEL sidecar enabled
technical_notes: Design: module = composition of submodules: prometheus-server, grafana-helm, otel-collector-deployment, log-forwarder-daemonset. We're exposing only opinionated surface vars to reduce combinatorial permutations.
Storage migration: use a controlled snapshot-and-restore for TSDB when switching retention/backends. Implement pre-upgrade snapshot job and a reconcile job that validates series counts post-restore.
OTEL config templating: use jsonnet templates compiled during 'terraform apply' via external data provider where runtime vars (sampling, processors) are injected to avoid manual YAML edits.

Health gates: implement a health-check controller that runs three validators after apply: (1) collector readiness + last-export timestamp, (2) Prometheus TSDB series growth within expected delta, (3) sample-based end-to-end trace/log verification using a synthetic request generator and a dedicated test tenant.
Upgrade strategy: blue-green for Grafana dashboards, canary for collector config changes (traffic split using service routing), and rolling restart with PV attach ordering for Prometheus nodes.
Security: ensure KMS-encrypted credentials for remote_write and S3 secrets via secret controller; RBAC role templates for read-only Grafana service accounts.
Compatibility: collector builds must remain compatible with existing APM pipelines; provide a compatibility matrix in README and automated preflight checks in CI.
Observability of the observability stack: instrument module actions (apply/plan/upgrade) to emit events to a central audit log and a per-tenant debug Prometheus scrape target.

Terraform considerations: avoid complex dynamic blocks in root module; prefer single-purpose child modules with version pinning and upgrade notes. Use lifecycle ignore_changes for Grafana admin password managed externally.
Testing: unit tests for jsonnet templates, integration tests in CI that deploy to ephemeral VPC peered in sandbox, and long-running soak tests for retention and TSDB compaction behavior.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - CI: unit + integration tests for templating and provider calls (GH actions)
Stage 1 - Staging VPC: deploy module to staging; run synthetic traffic generator; validate health gates and smoke tests (metrics/logs/traces)
Stage 2 - Canary in production: pick 2 non-critical customer cells; apply module with canary flags; monitor for 72h for errors/alerts and run regression prompts
Stage 3 - Progressive rollout: expand canary per-week, automated rollback if health gate fails at any stage
Stage 4 - Backfill + migration: run TSDB snapshot/restore jobs for tenants that change storage backend; verify series parity before cutover
Stage 5 - Full rollout and deprecation: mark legacy per-tenant modules deprecated in docs and provide migration guide
